intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that neurodevelopmental disorder with or without macrocephaly (NEDMAC) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the SMARCA1 gene (300012) on chromosome Xq25-q26.1.

checks.evidence_quote: This study suggests that hemizygous variants impairing SMARCA1 function can cause XLID with other variable features, such as macrocephaly and ataxia, in men.

paragraphs.text: Neurodevelopmental disorder with or without macrocephaly is an X-linked disorder characterized by intellectual disability in affected males. Additional features vary and have included macrocephaly, behavioral difficulty, learning disability, ataxia, and speech delay.

paragraphs.text: In 2 unrelated males with X-linked intellectual disability, Nishimura et al. (2025) used exome sequencing to identify novel hemizygous mutations in the SMARCA1 gene. Patient 1 carried a nonsense mutation (Q599X; c.1795C-T, NM_003069.5) that led to nonsense-mediated decay. Patient 2 carried a missense mutation (R448L; c.1343G-T). Both mutations were inherited from the patients' unaffected, healthy mothers. Structural modeling suggested that the R448L variant might destabilize interactions between SMARCA1 and nucleosomal DNA, contributing to an aberrant effect of the mutant protein.

paragraphs.text: In a male (patient 1) with X-linked intellectual disability, macrocephaly, behavioral difficulty, and learning disability, Nishimura et al. (2025) identified a hemizygous c.1795C-T transition (NM_003069.5) in the SMARCA1 gene, resulting in a gln599-to-ter (Q599X) substitution. The mutation, which was found by exome sequencing, led to nonsense-mediated decay. It was inherited from the patient's unaffected, healthy mother.

paragraphs.text: In a male (patient 2) with X-linked intellectual disability, ataxia, and speech delay, Nishimura et al. (2025) identified a hemizygous c.1343G-T transversion (NM_003069.5) in the SMARCA1 gene, resulting in an arg448-to-leu (R448L) substitution. The mutation, which was found by exome sequencing, was inherited from the patient's unaffected, healthy mother. Structural modeling suggested that the mutation might destabilize interactions between SMARCA1 and nucleosomal DNA, contributing to an aberrant effect of the mutant protein.
